one_liner: Two-file C89 power-of-two FFT/DCT/DST library, about 2x KissFFT's speed; still slower than PocketFFT and FFTW.
what_it_does: Computes forward and inverse complex DFTs, real DFTs and DCT/DST types 2, 3 and 4 of any dimensionality for power-of-two lengths, in double precision by default or float with MINFFT_SINGLE. You build an auxiliary-data object once (minfft_mkaux_dft_1d(N), ..._2d, ..._3d or the any-dimensional maker), then call minfft_dft(x, y, a), minfft_invdft and the others in place or out of place, and free it with minfft_free_aux. The README says its transform definitions and data layouts match FFTW's, but the API is its own; there is also a Fortran 2003 module.
how_it_is_fast: The complex DFT is an explicitly recursive split-radix (2/4) decimation-in-frequency FFT with hand-unrolled leaves for N = 1, 2, 4 and 8 and a precomputed chain of twiddle factors stored in the aux object. Each level touches mostly adjacent memory, which the author credits for cache-friendliness. Real transforms and DCT/DST reduce to a half-length complex transform, and multi-dimensional transforms apply a strided 1-D routine along each axis through a temporary buffer. There is no explicit SIMD; the speed comes from fewer operations than KissFFT's mixed-radix code plus simple, compiler-friendly scalar loops.
when_to_use: You want a small, dependency-free, MIT-licensed FFT you can vendor as two files (minfft.c/minfft.h) into C or C++, and power-of-two sizes are enough.
Replacing KissFFT for power-of-two transforms: the author's plot shows minfft above KissFFT at every size from 2^1 to 2^20 (about 2x at N=1,024).
You need DCT/DST types 2-4 or multi-dimensional real transforms with no FFTW dependency (FFTW is GPL or commercially licensed).
Mixed C and Fortran 2003 codebases that want the same library from both languages.
Accuracy matters: the accuracy plot puts its relative L2 error near FFTW's and PocketFFT's (about 2.9e-16 at N=2^20, about half of KissFFT's 5.8e-16; derived from page data).
when_not_to_use: Non-power-of-two lengths: every aux maker returns NULL unless N is a positive power of two.

Peak throughput: the same plot has PocketFFT faster at 2^7 to 2^16 and 2^19 to 2^20, and SSE2 FFTW about 1.1x to 2.9x faster at every size; SIMD libraries (PFFFT, muFFT, KFR) or Notorious-FFT, which reports 1.08-1.13x over minfft, are faster.
Sharing one plan across threads: the aux object holds a scratch buffer that every transform writes, even though the API takes a const pointer.

Memory-tight settings: the README says it 'does not try to save memory'; a 1-D complex DFT aux takes 2N complex values, type-4 transforms 6N reals, and multi-dimensional transforms add a buffer as large as the input.

integration.min_toolchain: C89 (C99 complex used if <complex.h> is included first); Fortran 2003 for the Fortran module; the author's benchmark build used GCC 13.2.1
integration.platforms: any (portable scalar C, no SIMD or architecture-specific code)
integration.thread_safety: Separate aux objects can be used concurrently (no global mutable state seen in minfft.c); a single aux must not be used by two threads at once because its scratch buffer is overwritten on every call.

gotchas: Multi-dimensional inverse real DFT overwrites its input (README note), unlike the 1-D routines, which preserve input when run out of place.

minfft_cmpl is C99 double complex only if `complex` is defined (i.e. <complex.h> was included before minfft.h); otherwise, including in C++, it is a double[2] array, binary-compatible with std::complex<double> but needing a cast.
Dimensions for the 2-D/3-D aux makers are given in C (row-major) order; Fortran callers must pass them reversed.
Transforms are unnormalized like FFTW (no 1/N factor anywhere in minfft.c); scale the inverse yourself.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose minfft over KissFFT or meow_fft when your sizes are powers of two and you want DCT/DST types 2-4 and multi-dimensional support in a tiny C89 drop-in. Choose PocketFFT for arbitrary lengths or more speed, PFFFT/muFFT for SIMD speed, and Notorious-FFT if you want a slightly faster derivative.
verified_claims_summary: The author's gnuplot chart (benchFFT harness; per the README's test-environment section, removed in April 2024: GCC 13.2.1 -O2, one isolated core of an Intel Pentium Gold G5420 at 3.8 GHz, FFTW 3.3.10 with configure-chosen flags, KissFFT 1.3.1, PocketFFT 1.0) plots double-precision 1-D complex forward DFT Mflops for N = 2^1 to 2^20. Digitised, minfft runs 1.36x to 4.83x KissFFT (median about 1.96x), about 0.74x to 0.96x PocketFFT at most mid sizes, and 0.34x to 0.89x SSE2 FFTW (derived from page data).
status_note: Stale: code is mature and recent commits (to August 2025) are documentation only; MIT-licensed, two source files, one closed MSVC build issue, easy to vendor.
